issue.title: A new ticket cannot be created with an acceptance criterion that names no check to settle it
issue.description:
Gate: C27

**Plan of record:** [2026-09-13 Mechanical ticket closeout plan](<https://github.com/OmniNode-ai/knowledge-base-internal/blob/main/beta/plans/2026-09-13-mechanical-ticket-closeout-plan.md>) (kb#410, squash `99b9dbf`), section 13 step **5**, mechanism in section 6.

**Repo / surface.** `omniclaude` — the ticket-creation admission guard, its policy file, and its inventory contract.
**Size.** M. **Depends on.** Nothing. **This is the head of the critical path (5 → 6 → 7).**

## Why

This is the primary mechanism of the whole epic. A binding must be declared **before the evidence exists, by the party that knows the intent, and attributably**. Ticket-creation time is the only point in the lifecycle that satisfies all three: the author writes the criterion and its falsifier in one act, before any code exists, attributed to the creator with the ticket's own timestamp.

The guard already fires on the issue-save tool, is fail-closed, has no wildcard exemption, and already requires a criterion-binding line. This adds a fifth requirement to a surface that exists.

**Authorising ruling:** `docs/tracking/ROLLING_WORK_LEDGER.md:7466` — an author-declared falsifier written at ticket-creation time counts as the acceptance of the binding. Overrulable by the operator.

## Acceptance criteria

* **AC1 — an unfalsified criterion is refused, and the refusal names it.** A create whose description carries an acceptance criterion with no named falsifier is blocked, and the refusal message quotes the offending criterion. RED first: the same create succeeds today. — falsifier: a guard test that feeds a create payload with one falsified and one unfalsified criterion, asserts a non-zero refusal, and asserts the unfalsified criterion's text appears in the refusal output.
* **AC2 — positive control: a fully falsified create passes untouched.** A create whose every criterion names a falsifier is admitted with no change in behaviour. — falsifier: the same test with falsifiers on every criterion asserts the create is admitted, so the guard is proven not to refuse everything.
* **AC3 — a merge-state-read falsifier on a behaviour-shaped criterion is refused.** A criterion asking about behaviour whose named falsifier is a merge-state read is blocked, consistent with the proof-class rule in [OMN-18135](https://linear.app/omninode/issue/OMN-18135). — falsifier: a test pairing a behaviour-shaped criterion with a merged-state probe asserts refusal, and the same probe against a merge-shaped criterion asserts admission.
* **AC4 — the requirement is a hook in the same change, not a sweep.** The check ships wired into the pre-tool-use guard path in the same pull request that introduces it, with no allowlist and no opt-in flag. — falsifier: the guard's own inventory contract lists the new rule, and a grep of the change for an exemption or allowlist key returns nothing.
* **AC5 — a guard failure is legible enough that the remedy is cheaper than the workaround.** The refusal prints the criterion and the expected falsifier shape, so the fix is an edit rather than a disable. — falsifier: the refusal fixture's stdout contains both the criterion label and an example falsifier line.
* **AC6 — each criterion plus its falsifier is one independently hashable unit, and the hashing unit is documented in the policy file.** The syntax is machine-parseable: the guard exports one unit per criterion carrying its label, its canonical text, its falsifier and a hash of that text, so the later autobinder pins `criterion_hash` without re-deriving the parse from markdown, and editing one criterion does not disturb another's hash. Accepted from the closeout-plan-corrections lane's comment. — falsifier: a parser test that round-trips each criterion line to its label, falsifier and hash, asserts editing one criterion leaves every other hash byte-identical, asserts a re-wrap does not change a hash while a rewording does, and asserts a malformed criterion that names no check is reported with a null falsifier rather than silently hashed.

## Out of scope

Judging whether a declared falsifier is a *good* one beyond the proof-class rule. The residual — an author naming something trivially true — is stated in the epic and is not closed here.
